The GEMM is 2·M·N·K = 2·1024·18560·4096 ≈ 1.557×10¹¹ FLOPs.

I did not run this. The estimate assumes B300 dense BF16 peak of about 2.25–2.5 PFLOPS, and cuBLAS typically sustains about 65–75% of that on a power-limited part. That gives roughly 1.6–1.7 PFLOPS achieved.

The problem is compute-bound. Operand traffic is small (A is 8 MB, B is 152 MB, C is 38 MB), so HBM at roughly 8 TB/s adds only about 25 µs, which overlaps with compute.

With 256×256 tiles there are about 290 tiles over 148 SMs, which is just under 2 full waves, so wave quantization costs little.

At about 1.65 PFLOPS achieved, 1.557×10¹¹ / 1.65×10¹⁵ ≈ 94 µs. CUDA-graph timing removes launch overhead.
